ov: A legless lizard native to Europe: neither a worm nor a snake. Unlike snakes, it has eyelids it can close. It spends much of its time hidden under objects, and it can shed its tail to escape a predator, though the tail regrows only as a short stub.

why.h: It spends the winter months in an underground burrow.

rg: Western, northern and central Europe; closely related slow worms reach eastern Europe and western Asia.
fx: It may be the longest-living lizard: about 30 years in the wild, and one lived 54 years at Copenhagen Zoo.
Its young are born inside a thin, transparent egg membrane, which they break out of straight away.
